parsed.basis: Tucumán in northwestern Argentina inherits national protections including self-declared gender identity in law, an X marker on identity documents and passports, access to gender-related care in public and private plans, and life imprisonment for a killing motivated by gender identity, although that aggravating circumstance was not applied in the 2025 Diana Sacayán ruling and the national anti-discrimination agency was abolished in 2024. Locally, the province is more socially conservative and religious than Buenos Aires, with less visible trans community infrastructure, no documented local anti-discrimination coverage comparable to Buenos Aires city or Rosario, and thinner practical recourse in San Miguel de Tucumán and rural areas. There is no criminalisation of gender expression or local facility ban, but a visitor who is outed faces greater street harassment, misgendering and service friction, with police and clinic responsiveness more uneven than in the capital.
